top_stories.label: Top Stories
top_stories.ai_summary: Two big set-pieces framed the day: Iran pressed on with a dayslong state funeral for late supreme leader Ayatollah Khamenei — his successor conspicuously absent — while the US marked its 250th anniversary with a combative Trump speech and severe heat and storms. Markets and shipping edged back to normal as OPEC+ approved another oil-output rise and Strait of Hormuz exports recovered. Elsewhere, a super typhoon forced evacuations near Guam, Venezuela's earthquake toll climbed past 2,950, far-right protests flared in Germany, and wildfires spread across a baking Europe.

stories.headline: Iran holds day two of Khamenei funeral; successor stays away
stories.summary: Prayers were offered for late supreme leader Ayatollah Khamenei as huge crowds gathered in Tehran for a second day of state funeral ceremonies. Three of his sons appeared, but the man tipped as his successor did not, and Iran-backed Hezbollah and Hamas delegations attended.

stories.headline: US marks 250th birthday as Trump hails nation, blasts 'communists'
stories.summary: America's semiquincentennial spilled into a second day. President Trump gave a combative anniversary speech praising the US and attacking 'communists,' while fireworks and flyovers were disrupted by a dangerous heatwave and severe weather along the east coast.

stories.headline: OPEC+ approves further oil-output rise as Hormuz exports recover
stories.summary: OPEC+ agreed to another increase in oil production as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz began returning to normal following the recent Iran conflict. Qatar separately said all its maritime activities would resume immediately.

stories.headline: Evacuations under way in Guam as super typhoon Bavi nears
stories.summary: Authorities ordered evacuations in Guam as super typhoon Bavi approached the Pacific island, threatening destructive winds and heavy rain.

stories.headline: Zelensky says he spoke to Trump; Kremlin says Trump offered to help Putin
stories.summary: President Zelensky said he had spoken with President Trump and called for 'American resolve' to help end the war. A Kremlin aide said Trump had offered by phone to help President Putin find a deal — even as Ukraine pressed deep strikes inside Russia.

stories.headline: Venezuela earthquake death toll rises past 2,950
stories.summary: The death toll from the earthquakes in Venezuela rose to 2,954 as rescuers pressed on, with anguished families left to identify victims at makeshift morgues. One survivor recounted days trapped beneath the rubble.

stories.headline: Thousands protest in Germany as far-right AfD eyes power
stories.summary: Thousands demonstrated across Germany as the far-right AfD set its sights on governing, and Germany's defence minister raised the alarm over the possibility of a far-right state government.

stories.headline: Wildfires devastate forests as Europe's heat returns
stories.summary: Infernos tore through forests in Portugal and elsewhere as temperatures climbed again across Europe, with hundreds of firefighters battling blazes amid renewed extreme heat.

stories.headline: Houthi attack kills 14 Yemeni government troops, officials say
stories.summary: An attack by Yemen's Houthis killed 14 government soldiers, Yemeni officials said, in a fresh escalation of the country's long-running conflict.

stories.headline: China frees prominent house-church pastor after Trump request
stories.summary: Chinese underground-church figure Jin Mingri was freed from prison, weeks after President Trump had requested his release. Jin, founder of the Zion Church, had been detained amid a wider crackdown on unregistered congregations.

singapore.label: Singapore
singapore.ai_summary: Stormy weather dominated the evening: seven people were taken to hospital, one unconscious, after a lightning strike at Pasir Ris Beach, with more thundery showers forecast (25-34°C). Police highlighted enforcement wins — more than 130 scam victims saved from losing over $2.9 million, and over 1,700 people placed under investigation after June's islandwide operations. PM Wong heads to Jakarta for a leaders' retreat with Indonesia, a new HarbourFront cruise terminal with biometric clearance opens July 7, and lighter talk ranged from 22,000 cicadas trapped in Tampines to 7-Eleven suing Nike over sneaker colours.

stories.headline: Pasir Ris Beach lightning strike: 7 hospitalised, one unconscious
stories.summary: Seven people were taken to hospital, including one man left unconscious, after being struck by lightning at Pasir Ris Beach amid thundery weather. It is a stark reminder to seek shelter during storms, which are forecast to continue.

stories.headline: Police, crypto exchanges save 130+ scam victims from $2.9m loss
stories.summary: Police and cryptocurrency exchanges stopped more than 130 scam victims from losing over $2.9 million, the latest in Singapore's push to intercept transfers before money leaves victims' hands.

stories.headline: PM Wong to visit Jakarta for Singapore-Indonesia leaders' retreat
stories.summary: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong will travel to Jakarta for the annual leaders' retreat with Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto, the two neighbours' key bilateral meeting.

stories.headline: New HarbourFront cruise terminal opens July 7 with biometric check-in
stories.summary: The new Singapore Cruise Centre at HarbourFront opens on July 7, offering airport-style biometric passport clearance, more dining options and ferry links to Batam and Bintan.

stories.headline: Over 1,700 under police probe after June islandwide operations
stories.summary: More than 1,700 people — 1,173 men and 603 women aged 15 to 85 — are under investigation following multi-agency islandwide operations conducted across Singapore in June.

stories.headline: Woman, 46, arrested over knife attack at Bukit Merah HDB block
stories.summary: A 46-year-old woman was arrested after allegedly attacking an acquaintance with a knife at a Housing Board block in Bukit Merah.

stories.headline: Man to be charged for spitting on police during Yishun fire response
stories.summary: A man will be charged after allegedly insulting and spitting on police officers during a firefighting operation in Yishun.

stories.headline: 22,000 cicadas trapped in Tampines Changkat as pilot curbs noise
stories.summary: About 22,000 cicadas have been caught using light traps in Tampines Changkat since March, and a task-force pilot has reduced the noise and disturbance for residents. Other towns are set to learn from the bug-control effort.

stories.headline: 7-Eleven sues Nike over Air Max in its orange-green-red colours
stories.summary: Convenience-store chain 7-Eleven is suing Nike, claiming an Air Max sneaker uses the orange, green and red colour scheme associated with its Slurpee brand.

stories.headline: Sembawang, Punggol residents had longest work commutes in 2025
stories.summary: Residents of Sembawang, Bukit Panjang, Punggol and Sengkang took the longest to travel to work in 2025, according to a survey — fuel for a familiar Singaporean gripe about commuting from the fringes.

wars.label: Wars & Conflicts
wars.ai_summary: On Ukraine, diplomacy and escalation ran side by side: Zelensky said he spoke to Trump and urged 'American resolve,' a Kremlin aide said Trump offered to help Putin reach a deal, yet Kyiv struck a major oil terminal near St Petersburg. In the Gulf, a fragile post-war calm holds — Iran is deep into a dayslong funeral for late supreme leader Khamenei, Qatar reopened all maritime activity, and Tehran floated preferential Hormuz transit fees as OPEC+ lifted output and exports recovered. Gaza's ceasefire is holding but strained.

theatres.name: Russia-Ukraine War
theatres.status: Diplomacy stirs (Zelensky-Trump call, Trump-Putin offer) even as Ukraine escalates deep strikes near St Petersburg.

timeline.event: Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, beginning the largest land war in Europe since 1945 (context).
Ukraine said Russia had damaged more than 200 railway locomotives in 2026, part of a sustained campaign against Ukrainian rail logistics.
Ukraine struck an oil terminal and the Baltic port of Vysotsk near St Petersburg in one of its largest deep strikes; Kyiv dismissed Russia's claim to have captured Kostiantynivka as 'a lie.'

President Zelensky said he had spoken to President Trump and called for 'American resolve' to help end the war; a Kremlin aide said Trump offered over the phone to help President Putin find a deal with Ukraine.

theatres.name: US/Israel-Iran (Strait of Hormuz)
theatres.status: Fragile post-war calm — Iran holds a dayslong state funeral for late leader Khamenei; Qatar reopens maritime activity and Tehran floats preferential Hormuz fees as exports recover.

timeline.event: A CMA CGM container ship struck by a missile in the Strait of Hormuz during the conflict may be sent for scrapping, its CEO said, underscoring the toll on shipping.

An Iranian envoy said 'friendly nations,' including China, would get special treatment on new Strait of Hormuz transit fees Tehran plans to levy; Qatar said all its maritime activities would resume immediately.
Iran held a second day of funeral ceremonies for late supreme leader Ayatollah Khamenei; three of his sons appeared but his expected successor did not, and Hezbollah and Hamas delegations attended.
OPEC+ approved a further oil-output increase as Strait of Hormuz exports began to recover, easing wartime disruption to global supply.

theatres.name: Israel-Lebanon / Gaza
theatres.status: Gaza ceasefire holding but strained; scrutiny persists over Israeli conduct after a detainee-abuse case.

timeline.event: Israel has not identified soldiers it acknowledged had abused a Palestinian detainee; two Gaza mothers believe the victim is their son, in a case highlighting scrutiny of Israeli conduct.

outbreaks.label: Outbreaks
outbreaks.ai_summary: The Bundibugyo Ebola epidemic in DR Congo and Uganda remains by far the gravest active outbreak — WHO's latest count (3 July) reached 1,481 confirmed cases and 454 deaths and is rising rapidly, overwhelmingly in the DRC, with 20 cases in Uganda and one imported case in France. A cruise-ship-linked Andes hantavirus cluster remains small and contained at 13 cases and 3 deaths, India is monitoring a single confirmed Nipah case in Kerala under tight contact-tracing, and WHO continues to flag elevated yellow fever risk across Africa and the Americas.

outbreaks.name: Bundibugyo Ebola — DR Congo & Uganda
outbreaks.status: Rising rapidly; concentrated in DRC, small spillover to Uganda and one imported case in France.
outbreaks.scope_note: WHO DON612 (3 Jul 2026), confirmed only: 1,460 DRC, 20 Uganda, 1 France (linked to DRC); 454 deaths including 2 in Uganda. Numbers rising rapidly since the 19 Jun report.

outbreaks.name: Andes hantavirus — MV Hondius cruise cluster
outbreaks.status: Small and contained; only limited human-to-human spread reported for this hantavirus.
outbreaks.scope_note: WHO DON611 (2 Jul 2026): 13 cases (12 confirmed, 1 probable) and 3 deaths (2 confirmed, 1 probable) globally, all linked to the Netherlands-flagged cruise ship M/V Hondius.

outbreaks.name: Nipah virus — Kerala, India
outbreaks.status: Single confirmed case under intensive contact-tracing; no onward transmission reported.
outbreaks.scope_note: WHO DON609 (25 Jun 2026): one lab-confirmed case in Kozhikode district, an adult male on ventilatory support; contacts under monitoring.

stories.headline: WHO: Bundibugyo Ebola tops 1,481 cases and 454 deaths, rising fast
stories.summary: WHO's latest Disease Outbreak News (3 July) reports 1,481 confirmed Bundibugyo virus cases and 454 deaths, up sharply since mid-June. The overwhelming majority are in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (1,460 cases), with 20 in Uganda and one imported, since-recovered case in France.

stories.headline: WHO details cruise-linked Andes hantavirus cluster: 13 cases, 3 deaths
stories.summary: WHO's 2 July update on the M/V Hondius outbreak lists 13 cases (12 confirmed, one probable) and three deaths globally, all tied to the cruise ship. Only limited person-to-person spread has been reported for this Andes-type hantavirus, and off-ship risk is assessed as low.

cybersecurity.label: CyberSecurity
cybersecurity.ai_summary: AI-driven crime took centre stage: attackers used an autonomous AI agent to run an entire 'JadePuffer' ransomware attack end-to-end, and a US government entity was reported to have paid $1 million to settle a data-theft extortion by the Kairos group. Software supply chains stayed under pressure, with North Korea flooding npm with malicious packages (108 in the 'PolinRider' campaign) and Google cutting off the 2-million-device NetNut proxy botnet. Fresh unpatched flaws also surfaced — seven bugs in the FatFs filesystem baked into millions of embedded devices, and a 'Bad Epoll' Linux kernel hole that gives unprivileged users root and also hits Android.

stories.headline: JadePuffer ransomware used an AI agent to automate the whole attack
stories.summary: Researchers detailed 'JadePuffer' ransomware in which an autonomous AI agent chained reconnaissance, exploitation (via a Langflow RCE) and encryption to run the intrusion end-to-end with minimal human input — an early real-world example of agent-driven ransomware.

stories.headline: US government entity paid Kairos group $1M in data-theft extortion
stories.summary: A US government entity paid $1 million to the Kairos extortion group after a data-theft incident, according to a report — a rare confirmed public-sector ransom payment.

stories.headline: North Korea publishes 108 malicious packages in 'PolinRider' campaign
stories.summary: North Korean hackers pushed 108 malicious packages and browser extensions to open-source registries in a campaign dubbed 'PolinRider,' aiming to steal developer credentials and secrets — the latest DPRK software supply-chain push.

stories.headline: Seven unpatched flaws found in FatFs filesystem in millions of devices
stories.summary: Researchers disclosed multiple flaws in a widely used embedded filesystem (FatFs) bundled into millions of IoT and embedded devices. The bugs are unpatched at disclosure, and the sheer install base makes remediation slow — defenders should watch vendor advisories.

stories.headline: 'Bad Epoll' Linux kernel flaw lets unprivileged users gain root
stories.summary: A newly disclosed Linux kernel bug dubbed 'Bad Epoll' lets unprivileged local users escalate to root and also affects Android. No CVE/CVSS was cited at disclosure; treat as a high-impact local privilege-escalation risk pending vendor patches.

stories.headline: New 'Avalon' malware framework packs CrownX ransomware
stories.summary: Researchers detailed 'Avalon,' a modular malware framework that bundles the 'CrownX' ransomware payload, giving operators a flexible toolkit for intrusions and extortion.

stories.headline: North Korea-linked npm packages mimic Rollup polyfills to steal secrets
stories.summary: npm packages linked to North Korean actors impersonated Rollup polyfills to trick developers into installing them, then harvested credentials and secrets from build environments.

stories.headline: ARToken PhaaS exposes EvilTokens' Microsoft 365 phishing toolkit
stories.summary: Analysis of the 'ARToken' phishing-as-a-service platform laid bare the EvilTokens toolkit used to bypass MFA and hijack Microsoft 365 accounts via token theft.

stories.headline: EU Parliament member probing spyware was hacked with Pegasus
stories.summary: A European Parliament member investigating commercial spyware was themselves compromised with NSO Group's Pegasus, underscoring continued mercenary-spyware targeting of officials.

stories.headline: Armored Likho targets government and power sector with BusySnake stealer
stories.summary: The Armored Likho group targeted government agencies and the power sector with a new information stealer dubbed 'BusySnake,' continuing its focus on strategic infrastructure.

stories.headline: Google disrupts NetNut residential proxy network of 2M home devices
stories.summary: Google disrupted the NetNut residential-proxy network, cutting off roughly two million infected home devices that had been abused to anonymise malicious traffic.

stories.headline: Ransomware crews lean on Citrix Bleed 2, BYOVD and supply-chain creds
stories.summary: Ransomware groups are increasingly chaining the 'Citrix Bleed 2' flaw, bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver (BYOVD) techniques and stolen supply-chain credentials to gain and keep access, researchers said.

stories.headline: PamStealer uses fake Maccy sites and PAM checks to grab Mac passwords
stories.summary: 'PamStealer' malware lured macOS users to fake sites for the Maccy clipboard app, then abused PAM authentication prompts to capture their login passwords.
